rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥarām is used figuratively for something whose existence is impossible, as in God's barring the two things from unbelievers.
rows.anchor: استعير الحرام للممتنع وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read with the forms ḥarima/ḥaruma, with both fatḥa and kasra reported.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( حرم ) و ( حرم ) ، بالفتح والكسر . وحرم وحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A town's destruction means that God resolved or decreed to destroy it.
rows.anchor: عزمنا على إهلاكها . أو قدرنا إهلاكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning means turning away from unbelief to Islam and repentance.
rows.anchor: الرجوع من الكفر إلى الإسلام والإنابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those decreed for destruction remain sealed in unbelief until punishment; only at Resurrection do they return and confess their heedlessness and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أن قوما عزم الله على إهلاكهم غير متصور أن يرجعوا وينيبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are sealed, so they persist in unbelief and die in it until they see the punishment.
rows.anchor: أنهم مطبوع على قلوبهم فلا يزالون على كفرهم ويموتون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading inhum with kasra requires completing the prior sentence and supplying an omitted demonstrative for the righteous deeds mentioned there.
rows.anchor: إنهم ) بالكسر . وحق هذا أن يتم الكلام قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading can likewise be causal, meaning that they do not return; on the first analysis, ʿalā is not syntactically connected.
rows.anchor: بالفتح يصح حملها على هذا ؟ أي : لأنهم لا يرجعون ولا صلة على الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā attaches to ḥarām as its endpoint: their inability to return lasts until Resurrection, after which a conditional sentence is quoted.
rows.anchor: وهي غاية له لأن امتناع رجوعهم لا يزول حتى تقوم القيامة ، وهي { حتى } التي يحكى بعدها الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted genitive is supplied before Gog and Magog (their barrier), just as the inhabitants are supplied with “the town.”
rows.anchor: حذف المضاف إلى { يأجوج ومأجوج } وهو سدهما ، كما حذف المضاف إلى القرية وهو أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading is reported with fatḥa in futiḥat, by analogy with the earlier reading of ahlaknāhā; another reads Ājūj.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فتحت كما قيل : { أهلكناها } وقرىء ( آجوج )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog are two tribes of humankind; a saying makes them nine tenths of all people.
rows.anchor: وهما قبيلتان من جنس الإنس ، يقال : الناس عشرة أجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to people being driven to the gathering, or to Gog and Magog emerging when the barrier opens.
rows.anchor: وهم } راجع إلى الناس المسوقين إلى المحشر وقيل : هم يأجوج ومأجوج يخرجون حين يفتح السد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥadab is a raised or elevated part of the land.
rows.anchor: الحدب : النشز من الأرض . وقرأ ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads min kulli jadath, meaning graves; the source contrasts the Hijazi thāʾ with the Tamimi fāʾ dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله عنه ( من كل جدث ) وهو القبر ، الثاء : حجازية ، والفاء : تميمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yansilūn is also read with a ḍamma on the sīn; nasala and ʿasala both convey moving quickly.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { ينسلون } بضم السين ونسل وعسل : أسرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden إذا can stand in a conditional apodosis in place of the fāʾ; when both occur together, they link the result to the condition emphatically.
rows.anchor: و {إذا } هي إذا المفاجأة ، وهي تقع في المجازاة سادة مسد الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using either “idhā hiya shākhiṣa” or “fa-hiya shākhiṣa” without the other particle would also be sound.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاءت الفاء معها تعاونتا على وصل الجزاء بالشرط فيتأكد ولو قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hiyā is indefinite or ambiguous in reference, then explained and specified by “eyes,” as in the parallel wording about wrongdoers whispering.
rows.anchor: ضمير مبهم توضحه الأبصار وتفسره ، كما فسر الذين ظلموا وأسروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā waylanā depends on an omitted “they say”; the saying is circumstantial to “those who disbelieved.”
rows.anchor: * يا ويلنا } متعلق بمحذوف تقديره : يقولون يا ويلنا ، ويقولون : في موضع الحال من الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads al-baʿth with a vowel; the commentary compares this pattern to al-jalb and al-ṭard.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن { من البعث } بالتحريك ونظيره : الجلب والطرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For anyone doubting resurrection, reflection on the stages of initial creation removes the doubt.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل : إن ارتبتم في البعث فمزيل ريبكم أن تنظروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿalaqa is a piece of clotted blood.
rows.anchor: العلقة : قطعة الدم الجامدة . والمضغة : اللحمة الصغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḍgha is a small piece of flesh, about the size of what is chewed.
rows.anchor: والمضغة : اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ . والمخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhallaqa means smoothed and complete, without defect; embryos vary in completeness, corresponding to human variation in form, size, and stature.
rows.anchor: والمخلقة : المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب . يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gradual transformations display God's power and wisdom and argue that the one who originated humans from unlike substances can restore them, a fortiori and more easily by analogy.
rows.anchor: وإنما نقلناكم من حال إلى حال ومن خلقة إلى خلقة { لنبين لكم } بهذا التدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the verb “make clear” without an expressed object signals that these acts reveal aspects of God's power and knowledge beyond human comprehension or description.
rows.anchor: وورود الفعل غير معدي إلى المبين : إعلام بأن أفعاله هذه يتبين بها

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads liyubayyina lakum with a yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : ليبين لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs are reported in variants with yāʾ or nūn and with indicative or subjunctive endings; nūn forms also occur in the following verb nukh’rijukum.
rows.anchor: ويقر ، بالياء وقرىء ( ونقر ) ونخرجكم ، بالنون والنصب

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads nuqirru with nūn and ḍamma on the qāf, deriving it from qarra al-māʾ, “he poured the water.”
rows.anchor: وعن يعقوب : يقر بالنون وضم القاف ، من قر الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indicative reading states that God keeps in the womb whatever He wills until delivery—six months, nine months, two years, four years, or whatever He decrees—and expels or miscarries what He does not will to remain.
rows.anchor: فالقراءة بالرفع إخبار بأنه يقر { فى الارحام ما * يشاء } أن يقره من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjunctive reading makes “keep” a second purpose coordinated with “make clear”: God retains whom He wills until birth, growth, and accountability.
rows.anchor: والقراءة بالنصب : تعليل معطوف على تعليل . ومعناه : خلقناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following singular “then that you reach maturity” supports the subjunctive construction, with the singular used to indicate the generic human kind.
rows.anchor: ويعضد هذه القراءة قوله : { ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم } وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that God brings each individual out as a child.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل : نخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashudd is full strength, intellect, and discernment; it is a plural-form word with no singular used, suggesting strength in multiple respects.
rows.anchor: الأشد : كمال القوة والعقل والتمييز ، وهو من ألفاظ الجموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die, while others reach senility and dementia, returning to the weakness and limited understanding of childhood; God's power both raises and lowers human capacities.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ومنكم من يتوفى ) أي يتوفاه الله { أرذل العمر } الهرم

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aged person quickly forgets learned information, even asking who someone is again moments after being told.
rows.anchor: من بعد علم شيئا } أي : ليصير نساء بحيث إذ كسب علما

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿumur with a quiescent mīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو : العمر ، بسكون الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāmidah describes earth that is dead and dry.
rows.anchor: الهامدة : الميتة اليابسة . وهذه دلالة ثانية على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving barren earth is a second proof of resurrection; God repeats it throughout the Qurʾān because it is evident and directly observable.
rows.anchor: ولظهورها وكونها مشاهدة معاينة ، كررها الله في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth stirs with vegetation and swells; the variant rabaʾat means that it rose.
rows.anchor: اهتزت وربت } تحركت بالنبات وانتفخت ، وقرىء ( ربأت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahīj means beautiful and pleasing to the viewer.
rows.anchor: البهيج : الحسن السار للناظر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absolute “distinguishing” can mean separating people both in their conditions and in their places, so their recompense and station will differ.
rows.anchor: الفصل مطلق يحتمل الفصل بينهم في الأحوال والأماكن جميعا ، فلا يجازيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view counts five religions, four belonging to Satan and one to the Merciful, and classifies the Sabians as a kind of Christian.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الأديان خمسة : أربعة للشيطان وواحد للرحمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes “He distinguishes between them” to mean that God judges between believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { يفصل بينهم } يقضي بينهم ، أي بين المؤمنين والكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating inna Allāh on both parts of the sentence adds emphasis; Jarīr's verse provides a parallel doubled إن construction.
rows.anchor: وأدخلت { إن الذين ءامنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة إن الله على كل شىء شهيد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarīr's line, “The caliph—God clothed him in a robe of kingship,” illustrates the emphatic repetition of إن الله.
rows.anchor: إن الخليفة إن الله سربله … سربال ملك به ترجى الخواتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both udhina and yuqātilūna are read in active and passive forms; the sense is permission to fight, with “fighting” supplying the omitted object of permission.
rows.anchor: أذن } و { يقاتلون } قرئا على لفظ المبني للفاعل والمفعول جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission came because the Prophet's Companions were wronged.
rows.anchor: بأنهم ظلموا } أي بسبب كونهم مظلومين وهم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Report 711 says Meccan polytheists severely abused the Companions, who came beaten or wounded to complain; the Prophet told them to be patient until after the Hijra, when this first fighting permission was revealed after more than seventy prohibitions.
rows.anchor: كان مشركون مكة يؤذونهم أذى شديدا ، وكانوا يأتون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من بين مضروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the verse concerned emigrants intercepted by Meccan polytheists, who were then permitted to fight them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في قوم خرجوا مهاجرين فاعترضهم مشركو مكة فأذن لهم في مقاتلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's assertion that He can aid them is a promise of victory phrased in the authoritative manner of rulers; the earlier promise to protect believers signals the same.
rows.anchor: والأخبار بكونه قادرا على نصرهم عدة منه بالنصر واردة على سنن كلام الجبابرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “except that they say” is a genitive apposition to “right,” stating that their sole alleged offense was professing God as Lord.
rows.anchor: أن يقولوا } في محل الجر على الإبدال من { حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same point is expressed in the question, “Do you resent us for anything but that we believe in God?”
rows.anchor: ومثله : { هل تنقمون منا إلا أن ءامنا بالله } ( المائدة : 59 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's repelling people by one another means empowering Muslims to prevail over unbelievers through struggle; otherwise polytheists would have destroyed other communities' worship places.
rows.anchor: دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض : إظهاره وتسليطه المسلمين منهم على الكافرين بالمجاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is that the Prophet's polytheist community would have overpowered Muslims and protected People of the Book and demolished both groups' sanctuaries.
rows.anchor: أو لغلب المشركون من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم على المسلمين وعلى أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read difāʿ with an alif, and lahuddimat is read with a lightened consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( دفاع ) ولهدمت : بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A church is called ṣalāt because prayer is performed in it; another account derives the word from Hebrew ṣlothā.
rows.anchor: وسميت الكنيسة ( صلاة ) لأنه يصلى فيها . وقيل : هي كلمة معربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supporting God means supporting His religion and His allies.
rows.anchor: من ينصره } أي ينصر دينه وأولياءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is God's unseen announcement of how the emigrants will conduct themselves in faith if empowered and given worldly means.
rows.anchor: هو إخبار من الله عز وجل بظهر الغيب عما ستكون عليه سيرة المهاجرين رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: ʿUthmān calls this praise before trial: God praised the emigrants before they performed the later good deeds.
rows.anchor: وعن عثمان رضي الله عنه : هذا والله ثناء قبل بلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some cite the verse as proof for the rightly guided caliphs, arguing that only the emigrants—not the Helpers or freed Meccans—received this authority with just conduct.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : فيه دليل على صحة أمر الخلفاء الراشدين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies those whom God empowers as the community of Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : هم أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes alladhīna accusative as an apposition to man yansuruhu.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { الذين } منصوب بدل من قوله من ينصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent parsing is genitive, with alladhīna following alladhīna ukhrijū.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه مجرور ، تابع للذين أخرجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All matters return to God's judgment and decree; this confirms His promise to exalt His allies and make their word prevail.
rows.anchor: ولله عاقبة الأمور } أي مرجعها إلى حكمه وتقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This includes animals subdued for riding on land, ships running at sea, and the other things God has subjected.
rows.anchor: ما فى الأرض } من البهائم مذللة للركوب في البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fulk is also read nominative as the subject of a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { والفلك } بالرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An taqaʿa means “lest it fall”; its not falling is only by God's will.
rows.anchor: { أن تقع } كراهة أن تقع { إلا } بمشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave human beings life after they were inert matter: soil, sperm, a clot, and a morsel of flesh.
rows.anchor: { أحياكم } بعد أن كنتم جمادا ترابا ، ونطفة ، وعلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakafūr describes someone ungrateful for the many kinds of favor bestowed on him.
rows.anchor: { لكفور } لجحود لما أفاض عليه من ضروب النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who unite the listed qualities alone deserve the name “heirs”; the next verse explains that they inherit al-Firdaws.
rows.anchor: أي { أولائك } الجامعون لهذه الأوصاف { هم الوارثون } الأحقاء بأن يسموا وراثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance here has the sense discussed in Sūrat Maryam.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الإرث : ما مر في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaws is grammatically feminine by construing it as al-janna; it means a broad garden containing kinds of fruit.
rows.anchor: أنث الفردوس على تأويل الجنة ، وهو : البستان الواسع الجامع لأصناف الثمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes God building Firdaws with alternating gold and silver bricks, musk within, and excellent fruit and fragrant plants; another version uses bricks of pulverized musk.
rows.anchor: روي أن الله عز وجل بنى جنة الفردوس لبنة من ذهب ولبنة من فضة ، وجعل خلالها المسك والأذفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabīthāt can mean vile speech said or circulated about wicked men and women, who themselves engage in vile speech; the same pairing applies to good people and words.
rows.anchor: أي { الخبيثات } من القول تقال أو تعد { للخبيثين } من الرجال والنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” refers to virtuous people, including ʿĀʾisha, cleared of the obscene falsehood that did not match her purity.
rows.anchor: و { أولائك } إشارة إلى الطيبين ، وأنهم مبرؤون مما يقول الخبيثون من خبيثات الكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “those” refers to the Prophet's household, cleared of what the people of the slander said.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أولائك } إشارة إلى أهل البيت ، وأنهم مبرؤون مما يقول أهل الإفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the vile and good ones as women: corrupt women pair with corrupt men, and virtuous women with virtuous men.
rows.anchor: وأن يراد بالخبيثات والطيبات : النساء ، أي : الخبائث يتزوجن الخبائث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “generous provision” here uses the same expression as the promise in 33:31.
rows.anchor: وذكر الرزق الكريم ها هنا مثله في قوله : { وأعتدنا لها رزقا كريما }

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha recounts nine distinctions: Gabriel showed her image; she was the Prophet's only virgin wife; he died in her lap and was buried at her home; angels surrounded it; revelation came with her present; she was the caliph's daughter; her vindication descended; and she was promised forgiveness and provision.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة : لقد أعطيت تسعا ما أعطيتهن امرأة : لقد نزل جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of tastaʾnisū is becoming at ease after the uncertainty of knocking at another's door; the phrase means waiting until permission is given.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه من الاستئناس الظاهر الذي هو خلاف الاستيحاش لأن الذي يطرق باب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an indirect, consequent expression for permission, as in the rule against entering the Prophet's houses unless admitted.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : حتى يؤذن لكم كقوله : { لا تدخلوا بيوت النبى إلا أن يؤذن لكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a kināya and iridāf: the ease of knowing one's status follows permission, so the expression is put in its place.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب الكناية والإرداف ؛ لأن هذا النوع من الاستئناس يردف الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sense is to inquire or investigate whether entry is wanted, from seeing something plainly; al-Nābigha's “on one observant of solitude” illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون من الاستئناس الذي هو الاستعلام والاستكشاف : استفعال من أنس الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Common expressions such as “look whether you see anyone” and “I looked and saw no one” mean that the speaker sought information; al-Nābigha's مستأنس is cited for the sense.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم : استأنس هل ترى أحدا ، واستأنست فلم أر أحدا ، أي : تعرفت واستعلمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead derive from al-ins, meaning to find out whether a person is present.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من الإنس ، وهو أن يتعرف هل ثمة إنسان

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
rows.claim: Asked what istī'nās means, the Prophet answered that a man says tasbīḥ, takbīr, or taḥmīd and clears his throat to alert the household.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنه : قلنا : يا رسول الله ، ما الاستئناس ؟ قال : يتكلم الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visitor should greet the household, ask “may I enter?” and repeat this three times; if permission is not granted, he returns.
rows.anchor: والتسليم أن يقول : السلام عليكم ، أأدخل ؟ ثلاث مرات ؛ فإن أذن له وإلا رجع

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā came to ʿUmar's door, requested entry three times, then left, citing the Prophet's rule that permission is sought three times.
rows.anchor: ( 742 ) وعن أبي موسى الأشعري أنه أتى باب عمر رضي الله عنهما فقال : السلام عليكم أأدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man asked to enter by saying “May I come in?”; the Prophet had Rawḍa teach him the proper greeting and request, then admitted him when he used it.
rows.anchor: ( 743 ) واستأذن رجل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : أألج ؟ فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لامرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic visitors entered others' homes after a morning or evening greeting without asking, sometimes surprising a couple together; God stopped this and taught a better, more decent practice.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل الجاهلية يقول الرجل منهم إذا دخل بيتا غير بيته : حييتم صباحا ، وحييتم مساء ، ثم يدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have abandoned this religious etiquette like a superseded custom, even when they know the revelation and Prophetic teaching; the author rebukes inattentive listeners.
rows.anchor: وكم من باب من أبواب الدين هو عند الناس كالشريعة المنسوخة قد تركوا العمل به ، وباب الاستئذان

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading reverses the order: “until you greet the household and ask permission.”
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله : ( حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say the wording was tastaʾdhِنū and the scribe erred; al-Zamakhsharī rejects this report as unreliable.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير : إنما هو حتى تستأذنوا ، فأخطأ الكاتب . ولا يعول على هذه الرواية

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy also reads “until you ask permission.”
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي : ( حتى تستأذنوا ) { ذالكم } الاستئذان والتسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālikum refers jointly to asking permission and greeting the residents.
rows.anchor: { ذالكم } الاستئذان والتسليم { خير لكم } من تحية الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dumūr is entering without leave; its derivation from al-damār (destruction) likens the offender to someone doomed because of the gravity of the act.
rows.anchor: والدمور وهو الدخول بغير إذن واشتقاقه من الدمار وهو الهلاك ، كأن صاحبه دامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town is Sodom, one of Lot's five towns; God destroyed four with their inhabitants and left one standing.
rows.anchor: أراد بالقرية ( سدوم ) من قرى قوم لوط ، وكانت خمسا : أهلك الله تعالى أربعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil rain was a shower of stones from heaven.
rows.anchor: ومطر السوء : الحجارة ، يعني أن قريشا مروا مرارا كثيرة في متاجرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh repeatedly passed the destroyed town on their trading journeys to Syria.
rows.anchor: يعني أن قريشا مروا مرارا كثيرة في متاجرهم إلى الشام على تلك القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated passage should have led them to see God's punishment and remember it, but they did not reflect.
rows.anchor: أفلم يكونوا } في مرار مرورهم ينظرون إلى آثار عذاب الله ونكاله ويذكرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not expect resurrection or its consequences because they disbelieve in it; the text uses “hope” for expectation, which belongs to believers.
rows.anchor: بل كانوا } قوما كفرة بالبعث لا يتوقعون { نشورا } وعاقبة ، فوضع الرجاء موضع التوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they do not hope for resurrection as believers do, since believers expect reward for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أو لا يأملون نشورا كما يأمله المؤمنون لطمعهم في الوصول إلى ثواب أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Tihami dialect, the expression can mean that they do not fear resurrection.
rows.anchor: أو لا يخافون ، على اللغة التهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first in is negative and the second is a weakened form of inna; the lām distinguishes the latter from the former.
rows.anchor: إن } الأولى نافية ، والثانية مخففة من الثقيلة . واللام هي الفارقة بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittakhadhahu huzuwan means “mocked him”; literally, they made him an object of ridicule.
rows.anchor: واتخذه هزوا : في معنى استهزأ به ، والأصل : اتخذه موضع هزؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt is quoted after an omitted saying; presenting “whom God sent as a messenger” as though conceded makes their contemptuous denial more sarcastic than “whom he claims is sent.”
rows.anchor: { أهاذا } محكى بعد القول المضمر . وهذا استصغار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that he nearly diverted them shows the Prophet's intense effort to persuade them and present signs, though stubborn attachment to idols kept them from Islam.
rows.anchor: وقولهم : { إن كاد ليضلنا } دليل على فرط مجاهدة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this construction lawlā restricts the meaning of an otherwise unrestricted assertion, though it does not do so syntactically.
rows.anchor: { لولا } في مثل هذاالكلام جار من حيث المعنى لا من حيث الصنعة مجرى التقييد للحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a threat: delay will not let them escape, and the promised punishment must reach them.
rows.anchor: { وسوف يعلمون } وعيد ودلالة على أنهم لا يفوتونه وإن طالت مدة الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question answers their accusation that the Messenger misleads them by implying that the one who calls him astray is already astray.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { من أضل سبيلا } كالجواب عن قولهم { إن كاد ليضلنا }

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: A report attributes the saying to Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: ويروي أنه من قول جهل لعنه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever God renews a reminder through revelation, they renew their rejection and turn away from it.
rows.anchor: وما يجدد لهم الله بوحيه موعظة وتذكيرا ، إلا جددوا إعراضا عنه وكفرا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing terms describe a progression: turning away entails denial, denial lowers the reminder's standing and invites mockery; anyone receptive to truth would believe and honor it.
rows.anchor: حين أعرضوا عن الذكر فقد كذبوا به ، وحين كذبوا به فقد خف عندهم قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming punishment is a warning that they will understand what they mocked when God's punishment strikes at Badr or on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: فسيأتيهم } وعيد لهم وإنذار بأنهم سيعلمون إذا مسهم عذاب الله يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they mocked is the Qurʾān; its reports and realities, hidden from them, will come to them.
rows.anchor: ما } الشيء الذي كانوا يستهزءون به وهو القرآن ، وسيأتيهم أنباؤه وأحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj is a plant kind; karīm describes what is pleasing and praiseworthy in its domain. A noble face, useful book, and the poet's “from his nobility” illustrate the sense of karīm.
rows.anchor: وصف الزوج وهو الصنف من النبات بالكرم ، والكريم : صفة لكل ما يرضي ويحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noble plant is one whose benefits are pleasing; the poem's word karami praises the subject's bravery and valor.
rows.anchor: حتى يشق الصفوف من كرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant is pleasing in the benefits associated with it.
rows.anchor: والنبات الكريم : المرضي فيما يتعلق به من المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diversity of plants is a sign that their creator can revive the dead; most people are sealed against belief and not expected to believe.
rows.anchor: إنبات تلك الأصناف { لآية } على أن منبتها قادر على إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in punishing unbelievers and merciful to those who repent, believe, and do good.
rows.anchor: وإن ربك لهو العزيز } في انتقامه من الكفرة { الرحيم } لمن تاب وآمن

words: كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull conveys comprehensive coverage of plant kinds, while kam conveys their immense abundance; together they point to God's complete power.
rows.anchor: قد دل { كل } على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات على سبيل التفصيل ، و { كم } على أن هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation limits the noble kinds to useful plants and leaves harmful ones unmentioned.
rows.anchor: يحتمل معنيين ، أحدهما : أن النبات على نوعين : نافع وضار ، فذكر كثرة ما أنبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, all plants, useful and harmful, are included and called noble because each has some benefit and wise creation has a sound purpose.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يعم جميع النبات نافعه وضاره . ويصفهما جميعا بالكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the plants are many, the singular āya can refer to the act of planting as one sign, or to each plant kind as a sign.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أن يكون ذلك مشارا به إلى مصدر أنبتنا ، فكأنه قال : إن في الإنبات لآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them “the wrongdoing people” before specifying “Pharaoh's people” marks them as unjust; the two labels are appositional restatements with the same referent.
rows.anchor: سجل عليهم بالظلم بأن قدم الظالمين ، ثم عطفهم عليهم عطف البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deserve the label for wronging themselves through unbelief and evil, and for enslaving the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وقد استحقوا هذا الاسم من جهتين : من جهة ظلمهم أنفسهم بالكفر وشرارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on the nūn, alā yattaqūni means “will they not fear Me?”; one nūn is deleted where two meet and the yāʾ is omitted, its kasra remaining.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( ألا يتقون ) بكسر النون ، بمعنى : ألا يتقونني : فحذفت النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may be an independent remark after Moses is sent, registering their wrongdoing and expressing amazement at their oppression and lack of fear of God's punishment.
rows.anchor: هو كلام مستأنف أتبعه عز وجل إرساله إليهم للإنذار ، والتسجيل عليهم بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, yattaqūna is a circumstantial clause describing the wrongdoers as unjust without fearing God or His punishment.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون { لا يتقون } حالا من الضمير في الظالمين ، أي : يظلمون غير متقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person reading alā tattaqūna shifts to direct address, confronting and angrily rebuking Pharaoh's people; the author illustrates it with an accuser turning to scold the culprit present.
rows.anchor: وأما من قرأ : ألا تتقون . على الخطاب . فعلى طريقة الالتفات إليهم ، وجبههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing absent recipients during Moses's private colloquy is like speaking in their presence because Moses will convey it; the wording urges him toward piety and gives believers lessons from verses about unbelievers.
rows.anchor: إجراء ذلك في تكليم المرسل إليهم في معنى إجرائه بحضرتهم وإلقائه إلى مسامعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis of the yāʾ reading with kasra takes it as alā yā nāsi ittaqūn, “People, will you not fear Me?”, compared with the address in 2:34.
rows.anchor: وفي { ألا يتقون } بالياء وكسر النون وجه آخر ، وهو أن يكون المعنى : ألا يا ناس اتقون
